output.summary: The backlog growth is driven mainly by the per-agent close quota, which induced premature closes, ticket splitting and quick-ticket picking. Created tickets rose mostly through split children and customer duplicates; first-contact demand rose only about 4%, and closes per agent rose from 11.7 to 19.0, so demand and capacity explanations are contradicted. The 14-day reopen rise is real, not a configuration artifact: the trigger is unchanged since 2024 and courtesy-only replies are about 5%. The Payroll launch is contradicted because the backlog began growing in July, before its August release, and Payroll tickets are a small share of the backlog. Whether engineering bugs drive the aged complex tickets is unknown. Recommended: suspend the quota in favour of quality measures, run the blocking-status classification, and do not approve the 12 hires or the quota increase. Confidence is moderate because the bug link is unmeasured.
